title: Signal Truce
premise: A neon-styled real-time territory conquest game where each region on a Europe-like command map broadcasts as its own faction and the player fights to dominate the network.
interaction_model: Mouse or touch selection plus drag-and-release troop routing between adjacent regions, supported by HUD buttons for pause, speed, music, and a defensive jammer ability.
objective: Choose a starting hub, expand through connected territories, capture enemy capitals to annex whole factions, and take control of every region on the map.
progression: Begins with start-position selection, escalates into multi-front expansion and defense, then snowballs through capital captures until either the player is eliminated or all enemy signals are absorbed.
theme: Cyber command warfare framed as signal control over a stylized European network.
mood: Tense, futuristic, competitive, and slightly arcade-like despite its strategic pacing.
likely_audience: Players who enjoy accessible real-time strategy, territory control games, and streamlined map-conquest experiences on web or mobile devices.
confidence_notes: High confidence in the graph-based territory conquest loop because node ownership, adjacency, troop transfer, AI attacks, and annexation are explicit in code.
High confidence that the jammer button is a temporary defensive anti-raid mechanic because AI skips attacks into player nodes while `peaceActive > 0`.
Moderate confidence in intended inspiration; the code suggests a compact RTS/territory-control hybrid rather than a deep simulation.
recreation_prompt: Create a single-screen browser strategy game called 'Signal Truce' where the player fights for control of a stylized Europe-like network map made of connected polygon regions. Present it as a cyber command conflict with glowing neon UI, dark sci-fi panels, a full-screen canvas map, and a HUD layered on top. At the start, let the player tap or click any region to claim it as their opening command hub, then begin a real-time match where every other region belongs to its own rival faction. Each region should generate troops over time up to a capacity limit, and the player should drag from one owned region to an adjacent connected region to send half its troops as a moving packet across the link. If troops reach a friendly region they reinforce it; if they reach an enemy or neutral region they subtract from its count until it is captured. Mark each faction's starting region as a capital, and when a capital falls, instantly annex that entire faction so all of its remaining regions and moving troops switch to the winner. Include AI factions that periodically evaluate neighboring regions and launch attacks or reinforcements automatically, creating constant multi-front pressure. Add a special jammer ability called Signal Burst that temporarily prevents enemy raids into player-held regions and then goes on cooldown. Include speed controls, pause/resume, music toggles, animated event feedback, victory and defeat screens, and readable troop counts over every region. The overall feel should be a fast, readable, mobile-friendly real-time territory domination game with strong cyber-war presentation and decisive snowball swings around capital captures.
